survivors.name: Local scope map
survivors.description: See the captured business, account and phone relationships for an explicitly selected scope, including gaps and shared-account roles.
survivors.evidence: The live accounts schema distinguishes owned/shared accounts, account roles and parent WhatsApp accounts; phone discovery supports a number-specific account resolution. Cursor plugin documentation requires explicit account/phone context.
survivors.proof: This uses saved whatsapp_biz_businesses, whatsapp_biz_accounts and whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers responses and their capture-scope metadata to join known relationships and expose unresolved links with no external dependencies.
survivors.long_description: Use this command to inspect captured business, account and phone relationships for an explicitly selected scope. Do NOT use it for historical configuration changes; use 'ops changes' instead.
survivors.weekly_use: The agency maintainer checks the chosen account and number before the weekly integration work described in the brief; frequency is a role-based inference, not interview evidence.
survivors.leverage: A local cross-entity relationship view, not an alias for one discovery tool.
survivors.implementation_notes: Require explicit chosen scope; never infer that Bobe selected one of the discovered businesses. Preserve separate owned/shared relations, capture time, incomplete pages and unknown links. Do not equate prerequisites_met with readiness.

survivors.name: Captured asset changes
survivors.description: Compare two captures of the same selected scope and see changed fields, additions and evidence gaps without mistaking incomplete pages for deletions.
survivors.evidence: Live onboarding_status exposes per-app and per-account state, done/todo/unknown checks and capped pages; the brief identifies resuming setup and template review as repeated rituals. PyWa issues #221 and #214 show that absent fields can reflect contract changes rather than real entity removal.
survivors.proof: This uses two locally stored, time-stamped MCP response snapshots with identical business/app/account/filter scope to compute structural changes and completeness-aware additions or removals with no external dependencies.
survivors.long_description: Use this command to compare earlier and later captures of the same selected business assets. Do NOT use it to inspect current captured relationships; use 'ops scope-map' instead, or use 'ops template-compare' for two templates from different accounts.
survivors.weekly_use: The integration developer compares the last captured state with the current capture when resuming weekly setup and webhook work; this follows the brief rather than measured usage.
survivors.leverage: Temporal evidence from SQLite cannot be returned by a single current-state MCP call.
survivors.implementation_notes: Require matching scope/filter metadata and explicit before/after capture IDs. When either capture is partial, missing entities or fields are unobserved, not removed. Never overwrite unknown with todo. Ignore only capture-envelope bookkeeping; do not silently normalize away API content.

survivors.name: Cross-account template comparison
survivors.description: Compare two explicitly chosen captured templates across accounts, with field and component differences tied to their original account and capture time.
survivors.evidence: Live get_template returns full state/category/rejection/component details and is account-scoped; live accounts distinguishes multiple account models and roles. No cross-account template comparison tool appears in the authenticated catalog.
survivors.proof: This uses two explicitly selected saved whatsapp_biz_get_template responses plus their account/template IDs and capture metadata to compute a field-and-component diff with no external dependencies.
survivors.long_description: Use this command to compare two explicitly selected saved templates, including templates in different accounts. Do NOT use it for a same-scope before/after inventory comparison; use 'ops changes' instead, or use 'ops template-checklist' for the values a template requires.
survivors.weekly_use: The template owner checks a reviewed template against its counterpart during the weekly template-operations ritual in the brief; cross-account use is inferred from the agency context.
survivors.leverage: It combines two account-scoped documents into a review artifact; the API offers only individual template reads.
survivors.implementation_notes: Require two saved template references; do not automatically pick by display name. Report returned identity/name/language only when present. Do not infer that a missing template is absent from an account whose capture was filtered or incomplete. A diff does not approve deployment or category choice.

survivors.name: Template component checklist
survivors.description: Extract the values a saved template needs and flag components the MCP send tool cannot express, without sending or inventing parameter values.
survivors.evidence: The live send_message contract requires reading template components first, separates body/header/button values, rejects richer unsupported component cases and forbids using review examples as recipient data. The live create_template contract supports named placeholders and richer buttons, so creation and sending have different capabilities.
survivors.proof: This uses a saved whatsapp_biz_get_template component document and the captured whatsapp_biz_send_message input contract to extract placeholder paths and supported versus unsupported parameter channels with no external dependencies.
survivors.long_description: Use this command to extract component and placeholder requirements from one saved template before composing a message. Do NOT use it to compare templates across accounts; use 'ops template-compare' instead. This checklist does not establish delivery eligibility or approval.
survivors.weekly_use: The template owner runs it when preparing template sends and reviewing template changes in the named weekly ritual.
survivors.leverage: Service-specific component interpretation produces an agent-readable requirements manifest, rather than renaming get_template or executing a send preview.
survivors.implementation_notes: Copy required values only from the user or actual business data; never populate from template examples. Keep body/header/button paths distinct even when placeholder numbers repeat. Extract named placeholders but mark any mapping the send contract does not establish as unknown/unsupported. Unknown component shapes fail closed. Do not check or predict service windows, pricing, payment readiness, approval freshness or delivery. Keep this to extraction and support classification; no full template renderer.

survivors.name: MCP catalog drift
survivors.description: Compare saved MCP catalogs and identify removed tools, new required inputs and changed schema paths that could break saved commands.
survivors.evidence: Official MCP documentation labels the server beta and evolving; live discovery returned 24 tools versus the documentation's 18. PyWa issues #221 and #214 demonstrate upstream field deprecation/removal as an actual integration failure pattern.
survivors.proof: This uses two locally saved tools/list catalogs and their exact input/output schemas to compute tool additions/removals, required-input additions and schema-path changes with no external dependencies.
survivors.long_description: Use this command to compare the upstream MCP tool contract between two saved catalogs. Do NOT use it for changes to business accounts, phones or template data; use 'ops changes' instead.
survivors.weekly_use: The integration maintainer can run the comparison during the weekly integration check and before updating scripted clients; the beta contract and observed documentation gap provide the concrete reason.
survivors.leverage: Local contract history and compatibility-oriented output are absent from a single tools/list response.
survivors.implementation_notes: Classify removed tools and newly required inputs as potentially breaking; show other changed schema paths without pretending to prove compatibility for arbitrary JSON Schema. Treat description-only changes separately. Compare the same endpoint/protocol catalog; do not call unrelated APIs.
